# package dissect

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/dissect"
```

Package dissect interprets CAN frames as CANopen messages by the predefined connection set (CiA 301 7.3.5, [canopen.Classify](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#Classify)): NMT, SYNC, TIME, EMCY, PDOs, SDO requests and responses, NMT error control (heartbeat, boot-up, node guarding) and LSS (CiA 305). In CAN FD frames it decodes the CANopen FD services (CiA 1301) on the same identifiers: USDO requests and responses, and the 20-byte CANopen FD emergency message. It is meant for bus monitors and traces.

[Decode](#func-decode) is stateless: each frame is decoded on its own. SDO segments do not carry the object they belong to, and the data segments of an SDO block transfer cannot be told from SDO commands by their content; a [Tracker](#type-tracker) follows the SDO transfers of every node and fills in both.

Devices may move COBs away from the predefined connection set (a PDO on another identifier, say); such frames decode by their identifier's default meaning, as Wireshark's CANopen dissector does.

Message is a decoded CANopen message. Exactly one of the service fields (NMT, SYNC, ...) is set, as Kind says, except for unknown frames and remote requests on PDOs.

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(f *canbus.Frame) Message
```

Decode interprets a frame by the predefined connection set. It never fails: frames it cannot interpret are KindUnknown, malformed ones carry an Error. CAN FD frames decode as USDO messages on the SDO identifiers and as CANopen FD emergency messages (more than 8 bytes, else as classical ones) on the EMCY identifiers; other CAN FD frames are KindUnknown.

### type Tracker

```go
type Tracker struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Tracker decodes frames like [Decode](#func-decode) and follows the SDO transfers on the default SDO channel of every node, so that it can attribute SDO segments to the object being transferred (SDO.HasIndex) and decode the data segments of block transfers (PhaseSubBlock), which [Decode](#func-decode) reads as commands. It must see every frame of a transfer, in bus order; a missed frame confuses it until the next initiate or abort. A Tracker is safe for concurrent use.

```go
func NewTracker() *Tracker
```

NewTracker returns a tracker with no transfers in progress.

```

```

### type USDO

```go
type USDO struct {
	// Client is true for a request.
	Client bool `json:"client"`
	// Dest is the destination address (byte 0): 0 broadcast, 1..127 a
	// node-ID, 0x80..0xFF a group; Destination names it.
	Dest        uint8  `json:"dest"`
	Destination string `json:"destination"`
	// CS is the command specifier (byte 1), Command its name; Remote is
	// set for the remote (routed) services, whose layout is not decoded.
	CS      uint8  `json:"cs"`
	Command string `json:"command"`
	Remote  bool   `json:"remote,omitempty"`
	// Session is the session-ID (byte 2).
	Session uint8 `json:"session"`
	// Index and SubIndex address the object (HasIndex: the message
	// carries them).
	Index    uint16 `json:"index"`
	SubIndex uint8  `json:"subIndex"`
	HasIndex bool   `json:"hasIndex"`
	// DataType is the data type byte of expedited and initiate messages.
	DataType uint8 `json:"dataType,omitempty"`
	// Size is the data size of an expedited message or a last segment,
	// or the size of the whole transfer in an initiate.
	Size uint32 `json:"size,omitempty"`
	// Counter is the segment counter.
	Counter uint8 `json:"counter,omitempty"`
	// TProc is the processing time per segment of a bulk initiate
	// response.
	TProc uint16 `json:"tProc,omitempty"`
	// Abort is the abort code of an abort, AbortText its description.
	Abort     uint8  `json:"abortCode,omitempty"`
	AbortText string `json:"abortText,omitempty"`
	// Data are the data bytes carried (expedited, segment; the rest of
	// the payload for a remote service).
	Data Bytes `json:"data,omitempty"`
}
```

USDO is a USDO message of CANopen FD (CiA 1301): a request (client to server, CAN-ID 0x600 + the client's node-ID) or a response (server to client, 0x580 + the server's node-ID). The sender is [Message.Node](#func-message-node); the destination is coded in the data.

#### func (USDO) String

```go
func (u *USDO) String() string
```

String summarises the message, e.g. "upload to node 5 session 3 0x1018:01"; it shows the first 16 data bytes.
